answer: Agents gain influence only after completing delayed trades with distinct counterparties whose balances have aged on-chain; new accounts start at zero weight, and splitting funds does not create maturity. A contract credits both parties after a challenge window and counts repeated links once. A sybil operator must lock capital across many identities and wait, paying opportunity cost while risking disputes. A cipher may hide trade details, but not collateral history; a marble-sized stake cannot quickly reach zenith influence.
